source.title: MERLOT RESERVE: Neural Script Knowledge through Vision and Language and Sound
source.authors: Rowan Zellers; Jiasen Lu; Ximing Lu; Youngjae Yu; Yanpeng Zhao; Mohammadreza Salehi; Aditya Kusupati; Jack Hessel; Ali Farhadi; Yejin Choi

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream task performance across model sizes and pretraining durations, a different measure from held-out language-model loss scaling. It does not test the original power-law or compute-allocation claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream VCR performance increasing with further pretraining and compares Reserve-B and Reserve-L on several downstream tasks. It does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy against parameter count, tokens, or compute; fit power laws; test prediction from small runs; or test compute-optimal allocation. Cited results from other studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: MERLOT Reserve is a multimodal video–text–audio contrastive model paper, not a scaling study. Kaplan et al. is cited only to justify FLOPs as the efficiency metric (fn. 8, App. B.3). There are only two sizes (B, L), and they also differ in vision encoder (ViT-B vs ViT-L), peak learning rate, FixRes epochs and finetuning learning rates. No loss-vs-scale curve, fit or prediction rule is reported. Figure 4 (VCR accuracy tracking pretraining epochs and contrastive validation loss) comes from one training run of a non-LM contrastive system, with a learning-rate-schedule confound the authors flag (fn. 7). None of these results measures what V1–V7 name, so they go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate on the scaling-related details, but those details are incidental. The authors' main conclusion is that joint pretraining on video frames, subtitles and audio with a contrastive span objective yields strong representations: state of the art on VCR, TVQA and Kinetics-600, and competitive zero-shot results, with audio helping. They note VCR accuracy tracks pretraining progress and might keep rising with longer training, possibly confounded by the LR schedule.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains multimodal video models with contrastive span objectives and evaluates downstream vision-language and video tasks; it does not use the original language-model held-out loss scaling recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance differs by model size on STAR; the authors also report that prompts and grammatical form can affect STAR results.

fits_no_version.finding: Finetuned VCR accuracy rises with pretraining epochs and tracks contrastive-span validation loss over 10 epochs (Fig. 4): +5% for B, +8% for L. The learning-rate schedule is a possible confound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multimodal contrastive video pretraining, downstream finetuned accuracy tracks pretraining validation loss within a run.

fits_no_version.finding: The larger Reserve-L beats Reserve-B on every finetuned task (VCR, TVQA, Kinetics-600). Size is confounded with vision-encoder size and training hyperparameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger multimodal video models improve finetuned downstream accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: On zero-shot STAR, Reserve-B beats Reserve-L; authors attribute this to prompt and grammar sensitivity of the larger model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-shot gains from model size can reverse through prompt sensitivity.

record.problems: The scaling-related evidence is limited to two Reserve sizes and reported pretraining progress on VCR; no scaling-law fits, uncertainty estimates, or extrapolation tests are provided. STAR gives a counterexample to monotonic improvement with size.
record.rows_left_out: Cited results from prior work and benchmark comparisons not involving Reserve's own scale or pretraining-progress results are omitted.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
Multimodal training, but no power-law form is tested.
No predictability analysis. There are only two confounded sizes, and the system is not a language model.

missing.what: Numeric zero-shot STAR, EPIC-Kitchens, LSMDC and MSR-VTT scores for B vs L, with and without audio (e.g. LSMDC 29.1 vs 31.0 with audio).
Confounds in the B/L comparison: different peak LR (4e-4 vs 3e-4), FixRes for 1 vs 0.5 epoch, different finetuning LRs, ViT-B vs ViT-L encoders.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V6 'supports' labels is overstated. Two confounded model sizes of a non-LM multimodal contrastive system do not test downstream predictability from scale or loss. Kaplan is cited only to justify FLOPs as the efficiency metric.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute is tested.
No power-law extrapolation from smaller runs is tested.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep or compute-optimal split is tested.
No controlled comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count is tested.
The study uses multimodal pretraining, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in this or other regimes.
The paper tests downstream results across a limited number of model sizes and pretraining durations, but does not fit or validate a general prediction rule from scale or pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents, compute-optimal split, or sensitivity of such fits to setup choices is tested.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Further pretraining on VCR and larger Reserve models on VCR, TVQA, and Kinetics-600
reader_labels.reason: VCR validation performance increases with additional pretraining (r1–r2), and the larger Reserve-L scores higher on the listed VCR, TVQA, and Kinetics-600 measures (r3–r14). These results support improvement in these tested settings, but do not establish a general prediction rule.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Reserve-B outperforms the larger Reserve-L, contrary to a consistent improvement with model size in this condition (r15).
